quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When entering public traffic from a driveway or private road, what should a driver do?

options.text: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
Assume other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Wait until it is safe, then merge into traffic.

questions.question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left?
questions.correctAnswerText: A green arrow pointing left
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can drive in the direction the arrow points. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steering ability
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions. Steering ability does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: Can be ignored in rain, snow, or ice.
Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Advisory speed signs show a recommended speed for driving through curves and turns safely. You should follow these recommendations, especially in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: What affects the space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space needed to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When should you NOT pass another vehicle?

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Never pass on hills, curves, at intersections, at railroad crossings, on bridges, or in any no-passing zone. Never pass a school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of the road with a median.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then proceed when the way is clear.
Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait for a green light or green arrow.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears (unless a sign says otherwise).

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?
questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the road, with the broken line on your side, when can you pass?
questions.correctAnswerText: If traffic is clear.
questions.explanation: When the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass if no oncoming traffic is in your way.

questions.question: When should you signal before passing another vehicle?

options.text: Early enough so others know your plans.

questions.correctAnswerText: Early enough so others know your plans.
questions.explanation: Signal early before passing so other drivers know what you plan to do in advance.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?
questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. Slow down when roads are wet, icy, or slippery. Driving too fast on poor roads makes it hard to stop and control your vehicle.

questions.question: What kind of blind spots do larger vehicles have?

options.text: The same blind spots as smaller vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Larger blind spots.
questions.explanation: Larger vehicles have bigger blind spots. Big trucks and SUVs have areas near the back that cannot be seen in their side or rearview mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake firmly.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral right away and press the brake pedal with steady pressure. Pull over safely and turn off the engine.

questions.question: What affects how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
How much time passes between drinks.

questions.correctAnswerText: All three of these.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, your weight, and the time between drinks. Eating slows down alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent impairment if you drink too much.

questions.question: When can you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your emergency flashers.
If no part of your vehicle is on the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except when there is an emergency.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
Passing poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.
Following the car ahead of you very closely.
Quickly changing lanes and weaving through traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and acting to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you see dangerous situations before they happen and take action to prevent accidents. It helps you deal with aggressive, careless, or impaired drivers and pedestrians.

questions.question: What does this sign warn drivers about?

options.text: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane ends and traffic must merge left.
questions.explanation: This sign means the right lane on a multi-lane road ends ahead. Traffic in the right lane must move left.

questions.question: What does an octagonal sign always mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop sign.
questions.explanation: All octagonal signs are stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people.
Certain turns are allowed from certain lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane is for vehicles with a certain number of people.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a high occupancy vehicle (HOV) lane. HOV lanes are reserved for buses and vehicles with a driver and at least one passenger, as shown on the sign.

questions.question: What happens if two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time?

options.text: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
The driver on the left has the right-of-way.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right has the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: If you reach an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle on your right, yield to that vehicle. You may then go when it is safe.

questions.question: To be ready for anything on the road ahead, you should:

options.text: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus only on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the entire road and all sides of the road.
questions.explanation: Good driving depends on seeing problems before you reach them. Look far ahead, but do not just stare at the center. Scan the entire road, including both sides.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means a ____ light will appear soon.
questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light means a steady red light is coming next.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue on a long trip, you should:

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Switch feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull off the road safely to nap or rest for the night.

questions.question: Always signal when:

options.text: Entering or leaving a parking space.
Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Always use your turn signal when changing lanes, entering or leaving a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area. Tell other drivers what you are doing to prevent accidents.

questions.question: Road signs that require drivers to obey them are called:
questions.correctAnswerText: Regulatory signs.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs require you to follow the instruction. Breaking the law on these signs can result in a penalty.

questions.question: Before starting the engine, you should:

options.text: Make sure only back seat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adult passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only child passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Before starting your car, buckle your seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: A flashing red light means:

options.text: The same thing as a stop sign.
You do not need to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which of the following does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgment of speed and distance gets worse.
You calm down and focus better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and focus better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, affects your vision, distorts your judgment of speed and distance, reduces how well you see headlights, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be on the road ahead.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, a pedestrian should walk on the:

options.text: Side of the road with lighter traffic.
Same side as the direction traffic is moving.
Side of the road with heavier traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road facing the traffic coming toward you.

questions.question: Where are you not allowed to park?

options.text: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
Within 12 inches of the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane. When parking on the street, you must stay within 12 inches of the side of the road.

questions.question: What affects how far your car travels before it stops?

options.text: How fast your vehicle is going.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Braking distance depends on your speed, the condition of your brakes and tires, and the condition of the road surface.

questions.question: What does an "End school zone" sign tell you?

options.text: You are entering a zone with a lower speed limit.
Pedestrians may be in the area.
The lower speed zone has ended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lower speed zone has ended.
questions.explanation: Follow the school zone speed limit during the times shown. An "End school zone" sign means you are leaving the area with the lower speed limit.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of your car without looking.
They will not cross unless with an adult.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of your car without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when children are near. Children may not understand danger and could run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
The road ahead turns sharply left, then right.
The road ahead curves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road will turn sharply to the right and then to the left.

questions.question: A driver under 21 with a probationary license can transport their dependents and how many other passengers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Up to one other passenger.
questions.explanation: Drivers under 21 with probationary licenses have passenger limits. They can transport their dependents and only one additional passenger.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers what they must or must not do. It means you cannot turn left at this location.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, pull safely to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, during bad weather, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: Your windshield wipers suddenly stop working in rain or snow. What should you do?

options.text: Roll down the driver's window and look out to see ahead.
Brake and pull off the road safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If your windshield wipers fail in rain or snow, slow down, turn on your emergency flashers, and pull safely off the road. Call for help if needed.

questions.question: What should you do when you see this sign?

options.text: Look for a train station ahead.
Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that railroad tracks are ahead. You must slow down when you approach railroad tracks. Trains cannot stop for cars, so you must wait for them to pass before you cross the tracks.

questions.question: You may cross solid yellow lines:

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making turns.
questions.explanation: Broken lines can be crossed, but solid lines cannot. You may only cross a solid yellow line when you are turning.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by ____ lines.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Solid white lines separate lanes going the same direction and mark the right edge of the road. Broken white lines separate same-direction lanes and can be crossed to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic going opposite directions.

questions.question: When driving in fog:

options.text: It makes no difference which lights you use.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Immediately pull all the way off the road and get back on when it is safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: Don't panic if your right wheels leave the pavement. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and carefully steer back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and making a small turn. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: If you are driving on the interstate and pass your exit, you should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a last-minute turn into an exit. If you miss your exit, go to the next one.

questions.question: You may pass another vehicle:

options.text: In a curve or on a hill because another vehicle is unlikely to be coming.
By using the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on a hill or in a curve because you cannot see oncoming traffic and may cause a collision. Never pass by driving onto the shoulder. Do not cross a solid yellow line to pass.

questions.question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: Vehicles at a four-way stop go in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: When you are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire tracks without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire tracks without stopping.
questions.explanation: Check that you have enough space to cross the entire tracks before driving onto them. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always check for trains before crossing any railroad tracks.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching. You should:

options.text: Ignore the signal if other lanes are available for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as quickly as you can.
Slow down, move your vehicle to clear the path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move your vehicle to clear the path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you must slow down, create a clear path, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.
